name: XFeat
plain: XFeat (Verlab, CVPR 2024): fast sparse keypoints and descriptors, matched by mutual nearest neighbours or LighterGlue; output as keypoints plus index pairs (the form COLMAP takes). Apache-2.0 code and weights.
summary: XFeat (Potje et al., CVPR 2024): lightweight sparse feature matching. A small CNN finds up to 4096 keypoints per image with 64-dimensional descriptors; they are matched as mutual nearest neighbours or with LighterGlue, a smaller LightGlue trained for XFeat. Returns both keypoint sets, the index pairs of the matches and their confidence.

papers.title: XFeat: Accelerated Features for Lightweight Image Matching

no_kernels_reason: not implemented: data-dependent keypoint counts (NMS, top-k, match filtering); the extractor is a small CNN
limitations: Sparse output: no dense warp. `result.matches()` gives the matched points for `estimate_pose`; `pairs` are the index pairs pycolmap / COLMAP databases take.
One image pair per call internally (batches run pair by pair); the keypoint counts differ per image.
No exportable module: the keypoint counts are data-dependent (`torch.compile` runs with graph breaks; ONNX / TensorRT export fails).
`xfeat` (mutual nearest neighbours) has no learned confidence: its scores are the descriptors' cosine similarities.
task_io: Input: two RGB images of one scene. Output: for every pixel of the first image its position in the second (x, y in pixels) and a certainty that the pixel is visible in both. Sparse matchers (LightGlue) return the keypoints of both images and the index pairs of the matched ones instead.

variants.name: xfeat

training_data.name: MegaDepth (Internet photo collections with SfM / MVS depth)

licence.training_note: XFeat: MegaDepth and synthetic warps of a 20k-image COCO 2017 subset (README training section). LighterGlue: trained with GlueFactory (README; MegaDepth, data not otherwise stated).

variants.input_size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32

portable.protocol: first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

original16.protocol: median of 5 after 3 warm-up, uint8 CUDA input, original code at the pinned commit, torch.no_grad; peak = max over the first call and the timed calls
original16.note: torch.autocast(float16) around the call; upstream XFeat.detectAndCompute + mnn, top_k 4096

quality.title: MegaDepth-1500, relative pose AUC@5 / @10 / @20 degrees
quality.protocol: Dense matchers: 5000 matches per pair sampled from the warp by certainty (upstream's balanced KDE sampling); sparse matchers: all their matches of one call (LightGlue, XFeat: LightGlue's MegaDepth-1500 setting; LoFTR, DeDoDe: their card defaults). OpenCV essential-matrix RANSAC (0.5 px threshold, normalised by the mean focal length); AUC of the larger of the rotation and translation-direction errors.

quality.title: MegaDepth-1500, every 5th pair, relative pose AUC@5 / @10 / @20 degrees
quality.protocol: Dense matchers: 5000 matches per pair sampled from the warp by certainty (upstream's balanced KDE sampling); sparse matchers: all their matches of one call (LightGlue, XFeat: LightGlue's MegaDepth-1500 setting; LoFTR, DeDoDe: their card defaults). OpenCV essential-matrix RANSAC (0.5 px threshold, normalised by the mean focal length); AUC of the larger of the rotation and translation-direction errors. The same 300 pairs for all modes, so float32 and bfloat16 compare pair for pair.

parity.text: CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 3e-05 vs the original. GPU, portable float32 and kernels float16 (the defaults): mean |diff| <= 0.0001 and p99 <= 0.001 (absolute error of the output `keypoints1`).
